findings.title: Timezone picker is inert: all 18 options are IANA names, and the clock parser accepts none of them — every displayed time silently stays on the host's timezone
findings.what_happened: Settings > Location > Time: I turned 'Use system time' OFF and set Timezone = America/Los_Angeles, then Asia/Tokyo, then UTC. app_settings.timezone and use_system_time persist correctly each time, but NOTHING on screen changes: the status-bar clock stayed 14:44 (host America/New_York) when it should have read 11:44 PDT / 03:44 JST / 18:44 UTC, the Dashboard header clock stayed host-local, and the Dashboard twilight strip stayed byte-identical (Sunset 23:48 / Astro dark 02:00 / Astro dawn 06:31 / Sunrise 08:43) across all three timezones. Root cause in source: packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/providers/clock_provider.dart:219 _parseTimezoneOffset accepts only 'UTC' or 'UTC+HH[:MM]' and returns null for anything else, so clockProvider falls back to SystemClock for all 17 IANA entries the picker offers. The fallback is completely silent — the file's own comment claims 'Failure to parse is explicit and logged at the Clock.fromUtc call sites', but nothing appears in app.log (grep for timezone/clock/tz over the whole 151-line log: zero hits).
findings.expected: Picking a site timezone must change displayed times, or the picker must not exist. clockProvider feeds imaging_service capture timestamps, session_provider and scheduler_provider, so a remote-observatory operator who sets the site timezone gets host-local timestamps on their frames and host-local scheduler decisions while the UI shows the timezone they chose.
findings.repro: Settings > Location, scroll to Time. Toggle 'Use system time' OFF. Set Timezone = Asia/Tokyo. Look at the status-bar clock and at Dashboard > twilight strip. Repeat with America/Los_Angeles and UTC.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rsg/24-status.png (LA, sys-time on: 14:43), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rsg/25-status.png (LA, sys-time OFF: 14:44 — unchanged), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rsg/27-status.png (Asia/Tokyo, sys-time OFF: 14:44), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rsg/31-status.png (UTC, sys-time OFF: 14:46 while `date -u` says 18:46), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rsg/28-crop.png (twilight strip unchanged under Asia/Tokyo). sqlite3 confirms timezone/use_system_time persisted each time.
findings.proposed_fix: Either store real IANA zones and resolve them with the `timezone` package (correct, handles DST), or change the picker to emit the UTC+HH:MM labels the parser already understands. At minimum make the fallback loud instead of silent.
findings.verdict_reasoning: Reproduced on display :85, fresh profile. Site set to Seattle (47.6062/-122.3321/1234 m). (1) use_system_time OFF with timezone=UTC (DB confirmed): status-bar clock 12:04:44 while `date -u` = 16:04:44 — unchanged host-local. (2) Timezone = Asia/Tokyo (DB: timezone|Asia/Tokyo, use_system_time|false): status bar still 12:05:48 while `TZ=Asia/Tokyo date` = 01:05:48. (3) Dashboard Moon card byte-identical across both timezones (Moonrise 00:55 / Moonset 13:24). Picker is inert on every surface reachable. Severity: the control is dead and the app displays a timezone it does not honour, but nothing it computes is wrong-by-timezone (LST/twilight are longitude-driven; capture timestamps stay host-local and self-consistent) — a dead-setting/false-claim defect rather than a night-costing one, so P2.
findings.location_wrong: The cited root cause only half explains the symptom. clock_provider.dart:219 _parseTimezoneOffset does reject the 17 IANA names, but 'UTC' — the one entry it DOES parse (Duration.zero) — changes nothing either: with timezone=UTC and use_system_time=false the status-bar clock still read 12:04:44 host EDT instead of 16:04 UTC. The real cause for the cited surfaces is that they never consult clockProvider: packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/shell/widgets/status_bar.dart:188/200/209 uses raw DateTime.now(), and only 6 call sites app-wide read clockProvider. A fixer who only widened the parser per the finding's 'where' would leave the status bar and dashboard exactly as broken.
findings.closure_evidence: VERIFIED CLOSED at source by lead: picker now offers kUtcOffsetTimezones (location_settings.dart:458), legacy IANA values auto-migrate via kLegacyIanaUtcOffsets (_migrateLegacyTimezone, :824-836), _parseTimezoneOffset handles the new format, and six display surfaces consume clockProvider (status bar temperature_and_time.dart:161, dashboard header, command bar, moon card, night timeline, standby).

findings.title: 'Use Device Location' is IP geolocation labelled as GPS, and it leaves the old elevation in place — producing a site that does not exist
findings.what_happened: The row reads 'Use Device Location / Get location from GPS'. Clicking it on Linux desktop returned 'Location updated: Newtown Square, Pennsylvania, United States' and wrote observer_latitude=39.9817, observer_longitude=-75.4072 — but observer_elevation stayed at 1234.0, the value from the previous (Seattle) site. The stored site is now a Pennsylvania coordinate at 1234 m; the highest point in Pennsylvania is 979 m. The success message says 'Location updated' with no hint that one of the three fields was not updated. Source: location_settings.dart:270 passes `elevation: settings.elevation` unchanged, and GeolocationService.fetchLocationFromGPS() (packages/skotiq_planetarium/lib/src/services/geolocation_service.dart:7-14) is not GPS at all — it does an HTTPS GET to the third-party service https://ipapi.co/json/.
findings.expected: (a) Do not call it GPS when it is IP geolocation — say 'Estimate from IP address (city-level, ~10 km)'. (b) Either fetch/clear elevation, or say plainly that elevation was not changed and needs review. (c) Disclose that clicking sends the user's IP to a third party before doing it — this is a silent outbound request from an app people run on isolated observatory networks.
findings.repro: Settings > Location > set elevation to 1234 and latitude 47.6062 (Seattle). Click the crosshair on 'Use Device Location'. Read the snackbar, then sqlite3 app_settings observer_*.
findings.evidence: Snackbar text captured via tree: 'Location updated: Newtown Square, Pennsylvania, United States'. sqlite3 immediately after: observer_latitude|39.9817, observer_longitude|-75.4072, observer_elevation|1234.0.
findings.proposed_fix: Rename the row, blank or refetch elevation alongside lat/long, and gate the network call behind an explicit one-time consent.
findings.verdict_reasoning: Reproduced. Set the site to Seattle 47.6062 / -122.3321 with elevation 1234 m (confirmed in app_settings and in the Rust log: 'Setting observer location: lat=47.6062, lon=-122.3321, elev=1234'). Clicked the crosshair on 'Use Device Location / Get location from GPS'. sqlite3 immediately after: observer_latitude|39.9817, observer_longitude|-75.4072, observer_elevation|1234.0 — coordinates replaced by an IP lookup, elevation left at the Seattle value. Independently confirmed the source: `curl http://ip-api.com/json/` from this host returns lat 39.9817, lon -75.4072, city Newtown Square, region Pennsylvania — exact match. The resulting site (Newtown Square PA at 1234 m; PA's highest point is 979 m) is indeed impossible. Severity P2: the mislabel and undisclosed third-party call are real honesty/privacy defects and the stale elevation is a real correctness bug, but elevation only perturbs refraction/horizon at the arcsecond level and the user still gets roughly the right coordinates.
findings.location_wrong: location_settings.dart:240-285 is right (the row, and `elevation: settings.elevation` passed unchanged). geolocation_service.dart:7-14 is wrong: those lines are fetchLocationFromIP's doc comment + signature. fetchLocationFromGPS is at :108-193 and is NOT 'not GPS at all' — it calls Geolocator.isLocationServiceEnabled/checkPermission/getCurrentPosition first and only falls back to IP (fetchLocation at :98-106) when that fails, which it always does on Linux desktop. Also the observed request was NOT ipapi.co: ipapi.co is rate-limited from this host (curl returns {"error":true,"reason":"RateLimited"}), so the app used fetchLocationFromIPAlternative at :52-95 — plain-HTTP http://ip-api.com/json/, a cleartext outbound request, worse than the HTTPS one described.

findings.repro: Fresh desktop profile, no pairing. Settings > Location > click the icon on the 'Sync from Server' row.
findings.evidence: tree captured the snackbar 'Location synced from server'; sqlite3 app_settings observer_* identical before and after the click.
findings.proposed_fix: Gate the row on isRemoteMode / a connected host, and word the success as 'Location read from <host>'.
findings.verdict_reasoning: Reproduced live on a standalone local session (status bar shows 'Local', no pairing). Settings > Location renders the 'Sync from Server / Fetch location from Headless Server' row enabled — location_settings.dart reads isRemoteMode at :103 but only uses it at :354, so this row is NOT gated. findings.title: Importing a detailed .hor horizon silently collapses it to 8 sector maxima — a single tree blocks a whole 45-degree sector
findings.what_happened: I imported a 36-point .hor file (one sample every 10 deg of azimuth, altitudes 10-29 deg). The snackbar said 'Horizon profile imported from test36.hor' and the eight compass fields filled in as N=25, NE=16, E=21, SE=25, S=29, SW=14, W=19, NW=23. Those are exactly the MAXIMUM sample in each 45 deg sector — the other 28 samples were discarded with no mention. Source confirms this is deliberate (location_settings.dart:498-501, 'highest altitude per sector wins'), but nothing in the UI says so.
findings.expected: Real horizon files from Stellarium/HorizonBox have 1-degree resolution and are the reason people generate them. Max-per-sector means one 29-degree tree at azimuth 190 marks everything from 157.5 to 202.5 as blocked, so the planner and Tonight will refuse targets that are actually clear — this costs imaging time on exactly the targets a southern-horizon site cares about. At minimum the import must say 'imported 36 samples, reduced to 8 sectors (worst case per sector)'. Better: store the full profile and interpolate.
findings.repro: Create a .hor with one line per 10 deg azimuth; Settings > Location > Local Horizon Mask > Import .hor / CSV; compare the eight resulting fields with the file.
findings.evidence: Input /tmp/ns-audit/rsg-files/test36.hor; resulting horizon_profile_json from sqlite3: {"N":25.0,"NE":16.0,"E":21.0,"SE":25.0,"S":29.0,"SW":14.0,"W":19.0,"NW":23.0} — verified by hand to be the per-sector maxima. Snackbar text captured from tree.
findings.proposed_fix: Persist the full sampled profile and interpolate at query time; keep the 8 fields as a coarse editor/summary. Failing that, report the sample count and the reduction in the success message.
findings.verdict_reasoning: Confirmed in source, which is decisive here. HorizonProfile.parseHorizonText (packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/providers/settings_provider.dart:567-603) parses every sample, then hands them to HorizonProfile.fromSamples (:539-555), which rounds each azimuth to one of 8 45-degree sectors (index = floor(((az+22.5)%360)/45)%8) and keeps only 'if (alt > altitudes[dir]) altitudes[dir] = alt' — the per-sector MAXIMUM, discarding every other sample. location_settings.dart:497-501 documents the reduction ('highest altitude per sector wins so an obstruction is never under-reported') and :526 shows the only user-facing message: 'Horizon profile imported from <file>' — no sample count, no mention of the reduction. Severity lowered to P3 because the app's horizon model is 8-sector everywhere (horizonDirections), so the reduction is intrinsic and conservative; the shippable defect is the silence about it, not a wrong number. Did not drive the native file-picker; the source path is unambiguous and the reported 8 values are consistent with per-sector maxima.

findings.title: Settings search sends autofocus queries to Files & Storage — the generated index for that page contains the whole Autofocus page's strings
findings.what_happened: Typing 'Backlash' in the Settings search box returns two sections and ranks 'Files & Storage' FIRST, above 'Autofocus'. findings.expected: A search for a setting's visible name must land on the page that actually contains it. As shipped, the search box's top hit for an autofocus term is a page where that setting does not exist — the user clicks it, finds nothing, and concludes the setting is gone.
findings.repro: Settings > search box > type 'Backlash'. Results: Files & Storage (highlighted/first), Autofocus. Click Files & Storage — no backlash control anywhere on the page.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rsg2/search-montage3.png (Backlash / Image output / V-curve / Disable guiding during AF all list Files & Storage first). Index dump of 'files-storage' shows the Autofocus strings.
findings.proposed_fix: Fix the index generator so a page's keyword list is built from the widgets that page actually renders; regenerate. Rank exact-title matches above subtitle/substring matches.
findings.verdict_reasoning: Reproduced offline against the shipped index plus the real matcher, then live. settings_catalog.dart:79-88 SettingsSectionDef.matches() ORs label/keywords/kSettingsSearchTerms[key]. Emulating it over the current generated index: 'backlash' -> ['files-storage','autofocus'] (files-storage first in sidebar order), 'v-curve' -> ['files-storage','autofocus'], 'disable guiding during af' -> ['files-storage','autofocus'], 'image output' -> ['files-storage'] only. Live on :84 typing 'Backla' into the settings search returned Files & Storage first, Autofocus second (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/v2sg/05-search-backlash.png). findings.location_wrong: File is right; the 'files-storage' entry now begins at settings_search_index.g.dart:257, not :247 (the generated index gained lines in a later fix wave).

findings.title: Settings search is a raw substring match, so any two-word phrase a user would actually type ('capture folder') returns 'No settings match your search'
findings.what_happened: Search 'capture folder' -> 'No settings match your search.' Search 'folder' alone -> Files & Storage, Autofocus, Image Grading. Search 'disk' -> no match, although the Dashboard's own empty-state text is 'Set a capture directory to track free space' and the status bar says 'No save path'. The matcher only finds a result when the typed string is a literal substring of one indexed phrase, so it cannot AND two words together.
findings.expected: Tokenise the query and AND the terms (NINA, macOS System Settings and Windows Settings all do this). The words the app itself uses elsewhere for this feature — 'capture', 'disk', 'free space', 'save path' — should all reach Files & Storage.
findings.repro: Settings > search box > 'capture folder' (no match); then 'folder' (3 matches); then 'disk' (no match).
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rsg2/search-montage.png panel 4 ('capture folder' -> No settings match your search.), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rsg2/search-montage2.png ('folder' -> 3 hits, 'disk' -> none).

findings.title: Files & Storage says 'Last backup: Never' while Settings > Advanced > Backup & Restore says 'Last Full Backup: Aug 2, 2026 10:30' — same app, same second, same fact
findings.what_happened: The scratch instance ran its startup backup check at 10:27:45 local: three .nsbackup files were written and app_settings got autosave.last_backup_at = 2026-08-02T14:27:45.635595Z. I then opened Settings > Files & Storage at 10:28 and scrolled to Status. At 10:30:02 the card still read 'Last backup / Never' with the trailing status 'Pending'. Clicking 'Back Up Now' immediately corrected it to 'Last backup / 0s ago' and 'In 23h', so the widget can render a real value — it just never picks up the backup the app itself performed. STRONGER REPRO: I then restarted the app (same profile, same DB). With autosave.last_backup_at = 2026-08-02T14:30:25.957100Z persisted and four .nsbackup files on disk, a freshly opened Settings > Files & Storage again reads 'Last backup / Never' and 'Pending'. So the persisted timestamp is never hydrated into the card at all; the only thing that makes it truthful is pressing Back Up Now in the current session, and that truth is lost on the next launch. DIRECT CONTRADICTION BETWEEN TWO SURFACES: in the same session and within seconds of each other, Settings > ADVANCED > Backup & Restore > Auto-Save Status reads 'Last Full Backup: Aug 2, 2026 10:30' and lists the real files under Recent Backups, while Settings > GENERAL > Files & Storage > Status reads 'Last backup / Never' and 'Pending'. Backup & Restore hydrates from the persisted key correctly; Files & Storage does not.
findings.expected: The Status card must reflect the persisted autosave.last_backup_at (and any backup completed in this session). 'Never' is a false statement about the user's data-protection state: the natural reaction is to assume backups are broken, or to conclude they are working when they are not.
findings.repro: Press 'Back Up Now' (card correctly shows '7m ago' / 'In 23h'), then stop and relaunch the app with the same profile and reopen Settings > Files & Storage: the card is back to 'Never' / 'Pending' while sqlite3 app_settings still holds autosave.last_backup_at and the .nsbackup files are still on disk.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rsg2/07-files-scroll.png ('Last backup / Never', trailing 'Pending') taken at 10:30:02; sqlite3 app_settings autosave.last_backup_at = 2026-08-02T14:27:45.635595Z; ls ~/Documents/Skotiq/backups shows skotiq_autosave_2026-08-02T10-27-45.572326.nsbackup. After clicking Back Up Now the tree reads 'Status / 0s ago' + 'In 23h' and the key becomes 14:30:25.957100Z. After restart (pid 2190911): tree shows 'panel: Status / panel: Never / panel: Last backup / panel: Pending' while sqlite3 gives autosave.last_backup_at|2026-08-02T14:30:25.957100Z and ~/Documents/Skotiq/backups holds 4 files from this run. Same-session comparison: tree of ADVANCED > Backup & Restore = 'Auto-Save Status / Last Sequence Save Never / Last Full Backup Aug 2, 2026 10:30' plus a Recent Backups list containing skotiq_autosave_2026-08-02T10-30-25.892145.nsbackup; tree of GENERAL > Files & Storage taken immediately after = 'panel: Status / panel: Never / panel: Last backup / panel: Pending'. /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rsg2/46-backup-restore.png.
findings.proposed_fix: Make Files & Storage read the same source Backup & Restore already reads (autoSaveStatusProvider, which seeds from the persisted autosave.last_backup_at) instead of the raw service status.
findings.verdict_reasoning: Both halves reproduced. (1) SAME-SESSION CONTRADICTION: with app_settings holding autosave.last_backup_at = 2026-08-02T16:03:47.621627Z (12:03 local, written by this process), Settings > GENERAL > Files & Storage > Status read 'Last backup / Never' + 'Pending' (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/vsg/23-files2.png), while Settings > ADVANCED > Backup & Restore in the same session showed 'Last Full Backup Aug 2, 2026 12:03' plus a Recent Backups list of real .nsbackup files. (2) 'Back Up Now' corrected the card to '0s ago' / 'In 23h' and the key became 16:15:01.581767Z. (3) STRONGER REPRO HELD: after stop+start on the same profile, with the key still 16:15:01.581767Z, Files & Storage again renders 'Never' / 'Pending' (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/vsg/24-post-restart.png). P1 stands: a false 'Never' about data protection is the cry-wolf class, and one of the two surfaces is lying at all times.
findings.location_wrong: auto_save_service.dart:149-166 is NOT where the bug is — that block is correct, carries a comment describing this exact symptom, and publishes the hydrated status. The hydration never reaches the instance the page sees: autoSaveServiceProvider (auto_save_service.dart:690) `ref.watch(backendProvider)`, so the service is rebuilt on a backend swap, while autoSaveLifecycleProvider — the only caller of start(config, lastBackup) — is read once, unawaited, at apps/desktop/lib/main.dart:280 and is never watched afterwards. start() also begins `if (_started) return;`, so a service started without arguments can never be hydrated later. Fix site is the provider wiring / the page's ref.watch at auto_save_settings.dart:179.

findings.title: Automatic backups are ON by default and write to ~/Documents/Skotiq/backups, a location the Files & Storage page never names and offers no way to change
findings.what_happened: 'Enable automatic backups' defaults ON with a 24 h interval and 'Maximum backups 7'. The page shows File Paths for 'Image output' and 'Sequences' and says application data is 'Managed automatically in Skotiq's application data folder' — but it never says where backups go. They go to getApplicationDocumentsDirectory()/Skotiq/backups, i.e. ~/Documents/Skotiq/backups, which ignores SKOTIQ_DATA_DIR entirely: this sandboxed audit instance, whose data dir is /tmp/ns-audit/r-settings-general/data, wrote its backups into the real user's Documents folder. 'Maximum backups' then PRUNES files in that undisclosed directory.
findings.expected: The Status section should show the backup folder path with a 'Reveal' action and let the user change it (backups belong on the same drive the user actually backs up, and an observatory PC's Documents folder is often the smallest volume). Retention that deletes files must name the folder it deletes from. Honouring the configured data directory is the minimum.
findings.repro: Fresh profile with SKOTIQ_DATA_DIR=/tmp/ns-audit/r-settings-general/data. Wait 5 min or press Back Up Now. `find /tmp/ns-audit/r-settings-general -iname '*backup*'` -> nothing; `ls ~/Documents/Skotiq/backups` -> skotiq_autosave_2026-08-02T10-27-45.572326.nsbackup and two more from this run.
findings.evidence: backup_service.dart:1025-1030 `_getBackupDirectory` = getApplicationDocumentsDirectory()/Skotiq/backups with no settings override wired up; observed files listed above; /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rsg2/07-files-scroll.png shows the Status card with no path.
findings.proposed_fix: Add a 'Backup folder' path row to Files & Storage (browse + reveal), default it under the app data dir, and show the resolved path in the Status card.
findings.verdict_reasoning: HALF of this is already fixed and must not be re-fixed. The path half is FIXED: backup_service.dart:1051-1055 _getBackupDirectory now calls the new resolveDefaultBackupDirectory() (:135-145), which resolves 'backups/' beside resolveDefaultDatabaseFile(environment) and therefore honours SKOTIQ_DATABASE_DIR. Verified live: this sandboxed instance wrote /tmp/ns-audit/v2-settings-general/data/backups/skotiq_autosave_2026-08-03T16-44-36.898434.nsbackup, and 'find ~/Documents/Skotiq/backups -newermt 2026-08-03' returns nothing. The disclosure half still reproduces: AutoSaveConfig defaults are backupEnabled=true, backupInterval=24h, maxBackups=7 (auto_save_service.dart:26-33), and the Status section (auto_save_settings.dart:306-372) renders only 'Last backup', 'Last error' and a 'Back Up Now' button — it never names the directory and offers no way to change it, while 'Maximum backups' prunes files in that unnamed folder. Severity dropped to P3 now that the cross-install/undeclared-volume leak is gone.

findings.title: INDI 'Test Connection' reports a green 'Connected. Found 0 devices.' for an address nothing can connect to
findings.what_happened: Settings > Connection > INDI Server Address > Configure. I set the host to 192.0.2.1 (RFC 5737 TEST-NET-1, guaranteed unroutable) port 7624 and pressed Test Connection: after ~6 s the dialog showed a green check and 'Connected. Found 0 devices.' I repeated with 127.0.0.1 port 9 (discard port, connection refused instantly): same green 'Connected. Found 0 devices.' A raw TCP probe of 192.0.2.1:7624 from the same machine hangs until killed, and nothing listens on 127.0.0.1:9. Nothing was written to app.log for either attempt (grep for 'address discovery failed' / '192.0.2' -> no hits).
findings.expected: Test Connection must distinguish 'reached an INDI server that reports no drivers' from 'could not reach anything'. On failure it should say so, and name the failure (timed out / connection refused / not an INDI server). The whole point of the button is to tell the operator, before dark, whether the address is right.
findings.repro: Settings > Connection > INDI Server Address > Configure > set host 192.0.2.1, port 7624 > Test Connection. Then host 127.0.0.1, port 9 > Test Connection.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rsg2/24-indi-test.png (192.0.2.1:7624 -> green 'Connected. Found 0 devices.') and /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rsg2/26-dlg3.png (127.0.0.1:9 -> same). `timeout 8 bash -c 'echo > /dev/tcp/192.0.2.1/7624'` exits 124 (hung). Root cause: packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/backend/ffi_backend/discovery_camera_operations.dart:86-102 `_discoverAddressDevices` catches every exception and returns `const <DeviceInfo>[]`, so the dialog's catch block at indi_server_dialog.dart:131 can never fire and line 129 always renders the success string. || RE-CONFIRMED 2026-08-02 on display :81 (profile r-settings-general) with two fresh cases: (a) 127.0.0.1:7624 with nothing listening (verified by 'ss -ltn' showing no listener on 7624) returned a green check and 'Connected. Found 0 devices.'; (b) host 'no-such-host.invalid' port 7624 - a name that cannot resolve in DNS - returned the same green 'Connected. Found 0 devices.' Screenshot: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rsg3/47-dialog-crop.png. Port validation in the same dialog DOES work (999999 -> 'Port must be between 1 and 65535.' and Save blocked), so the dialog validates syntax but never validates reachability.
findings.proposed_fix: Give the probe a result type that separates transport failure from an empty device list (or let _discoverAddressDevices rethrow for the explicit-address path, keeping the swallow only for background scans). Say 'No INDI server answered at <host>:<port>' on failure and 'Connected, but the server reports no drivers' on a genuine empty list.
findings.verdict_reasoning: Reproduced twice on my own display/profile. (a) Host 192.0.2.1 (RFC 5737 TEST-NET-1) port 7624: 'Testing...' for ~30 s then a green check with 'Connected. Found 0 devices.' — /tmp/ns-audit/shots/vsg/13-dlg-crop.png shows the host field reading 192.0.2.1 next to that message; from the same host `timeout 6 bash -c 'echo > /dev/tcp/192.0.2.1/7624'` exits 124 (hangs). (b) Host 127.0.0.1 port 9, refused instantly by the OS ('Connection refused'): identical green 'Connected. Found 0 devices.' — /tmp/ns-audit/shots/vsg/15-dlg-after.png shows host 127.0.0.1, port 9 and the green message together. Nothing logged for either attempt. Cause verified as cited and one level deeper: the Rust side is honest (native/skotiq_native/bridge/src/api/discovery.rs:153-168 map_errs the failure into SkotiqError::connection_failed); the Dart wrapper _discoverAddressDevices (discovery_camera_operations.dart:86-102) catches it and returns `const <DeviceInfo>[]`, so indi_server_dialog.dart's catch at :131 is unreachable and :129 always renders the success string. Both cited locations correct. P1 stands: the button exists solely to answer 'is this address reachable before dark' and answers 'yes' unconditionally.

findings.title: The Alpaca server address can never be set: 'Query Alpaca on startup' points at a 'configured Alpaca server' that no screen in the app configures

findings.title: Auto-Save & Backups renders compiled-in defaults instead of the saved settings, and changing any one field silently overwrites the other four
findings.what_happened: Before restarting, I set 'Enable sequence auto-save' ON (autosave.sequence_enabled=true) and 'Maximum backups' to 50 (autosave.max_backups=50), both confirmed in sqlite3. After an app restart with the same profile, Settings > Files & Storage > Auto-Save & Backups renders the DEFAULTS: 'Enable sequence auto-save' OFF, 'Maximum backups' 7, 'Last backup' Never — while the database still held sequence_enabled=true, max_backups=50, last_backup_at=2026-08-02T14:30:25Z. I then changed only 'Backup interval' from 24 to 12. sqlite3 immediately after: backup_interval_hours=12 (correct), but autosave.sequence_enabled had flipped true->false and autosave.max_backups 50->7. One edit to an unrelated field destroyed two saved settings, including turning a data-protection feature OFF, with no warning.
findings.expected: The page must render the persisted config, and an edit must be a partial update, not a full rewrite from stale in-memory state. As shipped, a user who configures this page loses it on the next launch and gets it silently reverted the moment they touch anything.
findings.repro: Settings > Files & Storage: turn 'Enable sequence auto-save' ON, set 'Maximum backups' 50. Confirm with sqlite3. Stop and relaunch the app. Reopen the page: switch shows OFF, Maximum backups shows 7. Change 'Backup interval' to 12. sqlite3: sequence_enabled=false, max_backups=7.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rsg2/39-autosave900.png (post-restart page: auto-save OFF, Maximum backups 7, Last backup Never) against sqlite3 output at the same moment: autosave.sequence_enabled|true, autosave.max_backups|50, autosave.last_backup_at|2026-08-02T14:30:25.957100Z. After editing Backup interval: autosave.sequence_enabled|false, autosave.backup_interval_hours|12, autosave.max_backups|7.
findings.where: packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/settings/widgets/auto_save_settings.dart:178-180 watches `autoSaveServiceProvider` (the raw service) rather than `autoSaveLifecycleProvider`, which is the provider that loads the persisted config (packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/services/auto_save_service.dart:783-810). _updateConfig at auto_save_settings.dart:68-84 does `service.config.copyWith(...)` and `_persistAutoSaveConfig` (auto_save_service.dart:854-861) writes all five autosave.* keys, so the stale defaults are written back over the saved values.
findings.proposed_fix: Have the page depend on autoSaveLifecycleProvider (await hydration, show a loading state) and make the persist step write only the changed keys.
findings.verdict_reasoning: Reproduced exactly as written. Before restart I set 'Enable sequence auto-save' ON and 'Maximum backups' 50; sqlite3 confirmed autosave.sequence_enabled|true, autosave.max_backups|50, backup_interval_hours|24. Stopped and relaunched the same profile: the page rendered compiled-in defaults — switch OFF, Maximum backups 7, Last backup Never (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/vsg/24-post-restart.png) — while the DB still held sequence_enabled|true and max_backups|50. Then changed ONLY 'Backup interval' 24 -> 12; sqlite3 immediately after: backup_interval_hours|12 (correct) plus sequence_enabled|false and max_backups|7 — one edit destroyed two persisted settings, including turning sequence auto-save off. Mechanism checks out: auto_save_settings.dart:179 does ref.watch(autoSaveServiceProvider) (raw service, defaults) and _updateConfig at :68-84 does service.config.copyWith(...) then _persistAutoSaveConfig (auto_save_service.dart:854-861) rewrites all five autosave.* keys from that stale object. The finding cites 178-180; the watch is on 179 — close enough to act on. P1 stands: silently disabling a data-protection feature the user explicitly enabled is data-loss-adjacent, not cosmetic.

findings.title: One failed 'Connect to Server' attempt drops the app out of Local mode permanently — every screen gets an undismissable red 'Error: not connected to server' banner and there is no way back without a restart
findings.what_happened: The app was running standalone: Settings > Connection reported 'Connection Status / Local' with a 'Local Mode' badge. I opened Connect to Server, left the prefilled localhost:8080 (nothing listening) and pressed Connect. It correctly reported 'Connection failed: Connection to http://localhost:8080 did not complete (state=disconnected)'. But after dismissing the dialog the app did NOT return to Local: Settings > Connection now reads 'Server Status / Not connected' and 'Connection Status / Disconnected', and a full-width red banner 'Error: not connected to server' is pinned under the title bar on EVERY screen (verified on Dashboard, Settings and Equipment). The banner has no close button, and the title-bar connection popover just says 'Connection Status / Not connected to a server' with no action. Nothing on the Connection page offers 'use local' or 'disconnect' — the only control is 'Connect' again.
findings.expected: A failed attempt to reach an OPTIONAL remote host must leave the local backend intact, or must offer an obvious 'Continue locally'. Standing up a scary red error bar on a machine that is working perfectly well locally is the cry-wolf pattern: the next time that bar means something, nobody will read it.
findings.repro: Fresh desktop profile, no pairing. Settings > Connection > Connect to Server > Connect (defaults localhost:8080). Dismiss the dialog. Look at the banner on any screen, and reopen Settings > Connection.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rsg2/30-banner.png and /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rsg2/31-dash-banner.png (banner on Dashboard); /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rsg2/36-connstatus.png (title-bar popover, no action); tree of Settings > Connection after the attempt: 'panel: Server Status / panel: Not connected / panel: Connection Status / panel: Disconnected' where it previously read 'Local' / 'Local Mode'. Banner condition is packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/shell/app_shell.dart:659-670 `ref.watch(sequencerBackendProvider) is DisconnectedBackend`.
findings.where: packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/shell/app_shell.dart:653-671; connection/backend swap in packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/settings/widgets/connection_settings.dart (Connect to Server dialog)
findings.proposed_fix: On a failed connect, roll the backend back to the local one instead of leaving DisconnectedBackend installed; add a 'Work locally' action to both the Connection page and the banner.
findings.verdict_reasoning: Reproduced on a desktop profile with nothing listening on 8080 (`ss -ltn`). Before: Settings > Connection read 'Server Status / Local' and 'Connection Status / Local Mode'. Connect to Server with the prefilled localhost:8080 correctly reported 'Connection failed: Connection to http://localhost:8080 did not complete (state=disconnected).' After dismissing, the page reads 'Server Status / Not connected' and 'Connection Status / Disconnected', and a full-width red 'Error: not connected to server' bar is pinned under the title bar — verified on Dashboard (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/vsg/27-dash-banner.png) and Equipment (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/vsg/28-equip.png) with no close affordance. The title-bar popover shows only 'Connection Status / Not connected to a server' with no buttons, and a full accessibility-tree dump of the Connection page lists exactly two buttons, 'Configure' and 'Connect' — nothing offers 'continue locally'. Extra contradiction not noted in the finding: the Dashboard header chip still reads 'Local' while the banner two rows above says the app is not connected to a server. P1 stands: on the machine that owns the hardware, one mistyped host permanently replaces the local backend (all role providers watch backendProvider) and leaves a standing red error on a rig that is otherwise fine.
findings.location_wrong: app_shell.dart:653-671 is exactly right (the banner keyed on `ref.watch(sequencerBackendProvider) is DisconnectedBackend`). The second half of the 'where' — connection_settings.dart — is only the dialog that calls ref.read(backendProvider.notifier).connect(...) at :472; it does not choose the post-failure state. The decision a fixer must change is packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/providers/backend_provider.dart:194-228 `_rollbackFailedConnect`, which installs a FRESH DisconnectedBackend on failure instead of restoring the previously-installed local FfiBackend. `useLocalBackend()` (backend_provider.dart:249-259, the only site constructing FfiBackend) has no UI caller at all, which is why there is no way back short of relaunch.

findings.title: The session checkpoint lives outside the database, so the app offers to resume a sequence its own database has never heard of — and the failure dialog contradicts itself
findings.what_happened: On launch, a profile whose database contains ZERO rows in sequences, sequence_nodes, sequence_runs, sequence_checkpoints, sequence_versions and captured_images was shown 'Recover Sequence? / A previous sequence was interrupted and can be resumed. / Sequence: New Sequence / Saved: 0m ago / Completed: 4 frames (0m integration)'. The claim of 4 completed frames is untrue for the database this instance is using. Pressing Resume produced, inside the SAME dialog: 'Recovery did not complete — Exception: No valid checkpoint to resume from' immediately followed by 'The checkpoint is still available. Retry resume or discard it to start fresh.' — two contradictory statements, one of them a raw Dart exception string, while the header still asserts '4 frames' were completed.
findings.expected: The recovery prompt must be scoped to the database in use (store the checkpoint in the DB, or key the file to the database identity), the frame count must come from that database, and a failed resume must not simultaneously say the checkpoint is invalid and still available.
findings.repro: Launch with SKOTIQ_DATABASE_DIR pointed at an empty scratch database while a checkpoint file exists at ~/.local/share/com.skotiq.desktop/skotiq_session.checkpoint. The dialog appears; press Resume.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rsg2/40-recover.png (the claim) and /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rsg2/41-recover-fail.png (the self-contradiction). sqlite3 on the instance's own DB: sequences 0, sequence_nodes 0, sequence_checkpoints 0, sequence_runs 0, sequence_versions 0, captured_images 0. The checkpoint file is at ~/.local/share/com.skotiq.desktop/skotiq_session.checkpoint — a fixed application-support path that ignores SKOTIQ_DATA_DIR entirely, exactly like the backup directory. HONESTY CAVEAT: HONESTY CAVEAT: this audit ran 8 concurrent app instances that all share ~/.local/share/com.skotiq.desktop, so the checkpoint was almost certainly written by a sibling instance. That is what makes the mechanism visible, but it is not required for the bug: the checkpoint is stored outside the database under a fixed path, so any user who repoints the database (app_settings has a database_path key) gets the same cross-database offer. The self-contradicting failure text and the raw 'Exception:' string are unconditional.
findings.where: packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/shell/app_shell.dart:398 (Recover Sequence dialog); checkpoint file writer (session checkpoint service, ~/.local/share/com.skotiq.desktop/skotiq_session.checkpoint)
findings.proposed_fix: Store the checkpoint in the database it belongs to (or stamp it with the database path/id and refuse to offer it to a different one), derive the frame count from that database, and replace the exception text + contradictory follow-up with one honest sentence.
findings.verdict_reasoning: Reproduced deliberately, without relying on the report's concurrent-instance accident. I pointed XDG_DATA_HOME at /tmp/ns-audit/v2sg-xdg (so getApplicationSupportDirectory resolves there) and planted one checkpoint at .../com.skotiq.desktop/skotiq_session.checkpoint with is_active=true, executor_state=Running, completed_exposures=4, completed_integration_secs=1200. SKOTIQ_DATABASE_DIR still pointed at the profile's own database, whose sequences / sequence_nodes / sequence_runs / captured_images tables all held 0 rows. On launch the app showed 'Recover Sequence? ... Sequence: New Sequence / Saved: 0m ago / Completed: 4 frames (20m integration)' — /tmp/ns-audit/shots/v2sg/60b-recover.png. That proves the mechanism: app_shell.dart:346-348 sets the checkpoint dir to getApplicationSupportDirectory(), which ignores SKOTIQ_DATA_DIR and SKOTIQ_DATABASE_DIR entirely, and the dialog's frame count comes from the checkpoint file (app_shell.dart:432-436), not from the database. WORSE THAN REPORTED: pressing Resume did not merely prompt — it STARTED THE RUN (executor went Running 'New Sequence', then Recovery started / DeviceDisconnected attempt 1/9) against a sequence tree the database has never seen (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/v2sg/61-fail-s.png). The self-contradiction half is confirmed in source but was not live-triggered here, because my planted checkpoint was genuinely resumable: app_shell.dart:437-446 composes, unconditionally whenever resume throws, SkotiqAlert(title:'Recovery did not complete', message: '$lastError\n\nThe checkpoint is still available. Retry resume or discard it to start fresh.'), and lastError is the raw caught object (runAppCheckpointRecovery, app_shell.dart:60-83), so a Dart Exception renders verbatim as 'Exception: No valid checkpoint to resume from' (sequence_executor.dart:1722) right above a sentence asserting the checkpoint is still available. Location app_shell.dart:398 for the dialog title is exact.

findings.title: At a ~900px window the status bar clips the third device chip mid-word instead of ellipsizing or dropping it
findings.what_happened: With the window resized to 900x800 the bottom status bar renders 'Disconnected  Disconnected  Disconnecte' - the third chip's final 'd' is cut off mid-glyph and its trailing state dot is missing entirely. There is no ellipsis and no overflow indicator; the text is simply sliced by the next element (the thermometer/temperature group).
findings.expected: An over-wide status bar should ellipsize the chip label, drop whole chips in priority order, or scroll - not paint a partial glyph. A cut-off word reads as a rendering fault and hides which device the chip belongs to.
findings.repro: Start the app, open any screen, resize the window to 900x800 (xdotool windowsize <win> 900 800), look at the bottom status bar.
findings.evidence: Live drive on :81, profile r-settings-general. Cropped capture of the bar: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rsg3/08-narrow-statusbar.png (900x36 region grab of the bar) and the full window /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rsg3/07-narrow-settings.png.
findings.where: packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/settings/widgets/... status bar row (bottom app chrome), status_rows.dart
findings.proposed_fix: Wrap each chip label in a Flexible with TextOverflow.ellipsis, and drop chips whole (lowest priority first) once the row cannot fit them, so the bar never shows a half-rendered word.
findings.verdict_reasoning: Resized the window to exactly 900x800 with xdotool and captured the bar (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/v2sg/43-bar900-2x.png). The third chip does render as 'Disconnecte' with the last glyph dissolved — but the stated mechanism is wrong: nothing slices it. status_bar.dart:419-455 puts the pill group in an Expanded > SingleChildScrollView with a ShaderMask alpha ramp over the last 24px, so there IS an overflow indicator, the content is reachable by scrolling, and the trailing readout group starts after the pill box, never on top of it. The claim's 'no ellipsis and no overflow indicator; the text is simply sliced by the next element' does not hold. Residual polish item only: the fade should stop at a chip boundary instead of mid-word.
findings.location_wrong: YES — badly. The named file packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/settings/widgets/remote_access_settings/status_rows.dart is the Remote Access settings status rows and has nothing to do with the bottom app chrome. findings.expected: A settings search should show the matching ROW ('Query Alpaca on startup - Connection'), and clicking it should open that section scrolled to and briefly highlighting that row. Index contents parsed from packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/settings/settings_search_index.g.dart.

(/tmp/ns-audit/shots/v2sg/07-glade.png), while the visible heading 'GLADE+ Galaxy Catalog' is rendered at packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/settings/catalog_settings_screen.dart:957. findings.title: The whole Settings section navigator is mouse-only: no tab stop, no focus ring, and every entry is exposed as a panel rather than a button
findings.what_happened: I clicked the Settings search box and pressed Tab 24 times, grabbing the sidebar region (230x580 at root 245,312) after every press and diffing it against the baseline: all 24 captures were pixel-identical (0 changed pixels, diff bbox None). Focus never lands on any of the 7 group headers or 35 section entries. Tab from the search box instead jumps to the window title bar - one Tab then Enter opened the 'Transient Alerts' popover in the top-right - and further Tabs go into the detail pane (three Tabs then Enter opened the UI scale dropdown). The accessibility tree agrees: every sidebar entry appears as 'panel: General', 'panel: Appearance', 'panel: Connection', while genuine buttons on the same screen appear as 'button: Test Connection', 'button: Save'. Source confirms it: _GroupHeader and _CategoryItem in settings_screen.dart are a bare GestureDetector inside a MouseRegion, with no Focus, no InkWell and no Semantics(button: true).
findings.expected: Every settings section should be a real focusable control: reachable by Tab/Shift-Tab, activatable with Enter/Space, drawing a visible focus indicator, and reported to AT as a button (or a selectable list item) with its selected state. Today a keyboard-only or screen-reader user cannot change settings sections at all.
findings.repro: Settings > click the search box > press Tab repeatedly. The sidebar never shows focus; the first Tab+Enter opens the title-bar Transient Alerts popover. Compare 'drive_linux.py tree': sidebar rows are 'panel:', real buttons are 'button:'.
findings.evidence: Live drive on display :81, profile r-settings-general. 25 region captures /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rsg3/kb-base.png and kb-1..kb-24.png, all identical by PIL ImageChops (changed_px 0, bbox None) for every one of the 24 tab stops. Title-bar activation captured at /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rsg3/56-kbd.png. Source: packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/settings/settings_screen.dart lines ~479 (_GroupHeader) and ~881 (_CategoryItem). Contrast that proves the app CAN do this: the main navigation rail uses NavItem (packages/skotiq_ui/lib/src/components/nav_item.dart), which is an InkWell - it takes focus and paints a highlight - so the rail is keyboard reachable while the settings section list beside it is not.
findings.proposed_fix: Replace both GestureDetectors with InkWell (or Semantics(button:true, selected:isSelected) + Focus + Actions) so they join the traversal order, paint a focus outline, and announce themselves. Keeping MouseRegion for the hover tint is fine - InkWell gives hover, focus and tap in one widget.
findings.verdict_reasoning: Confirmed both ways. Source: _GroupHeaderState.build and _CategoryItemState.build are a MouseRegion wrapping a bare GestureDetector — the whole file contains no Focus, no FocusableActionDetector and no Semantics(button:), and its only two InkWells (:755, :811) belong to _MobileGroupHeader and _MobileSectionItem, i.e. the mobile list, which is why the mobile variant is reachable and the desktop one is not. Live: clicked the settings search box and sent 15 Tab presses, grabbing the sidebar rect (root 385,300 250x600) after each; PIL diff against the baseline is bbox=None for all of them (the single non-None at press 15 is sub-pixel antialiasing on an already-selected row, visually identical). Tab does move focus — a whole-window diff changes on every press — it just never lands in the section list.
findings.location_wrong: Minor: the widgets are declared at settings_screen.dart:451 (_GroupHeader) / :470 (_GroupHeaderState) and :854 (_CategoryItem) / :873 (_CategoryItemState); the report's :479 and :881 are lines inside those build methods.
